title: Shared-basis Mirror compression of compositional motor option adapters
hypothesis: A shared rank-2 adapter basis with per-option Mirror coefficients retains unseen option-sequence behavior while using at least 25% fewer complete bytes than a full adapter bank and beats ordinary low-rank coefficient factorization.
physical_object: shared 8x8 motor core and common rank-2 residual atom bank
logical_multiplicity: eight composable motor options and held-out option sequences

task.teacher: shared orthogonal core plus option-specific linear residuals generated from a known rank-2 atom bank with one off-span option

fresh.release_rule: Keep fresh sealed if Mirror misses byte gate or native coefficient factorization exactly matches.

controls: native rank-2 shared basis coefficient table
top-2 atom selection with explicit indices
independent full rank-1 residual upper control
metrics: actual complete serialized inference bytes including shared core, atoms, IDs, sequence metadata
success_gate: Heldout sequence nRMSE <=0.02, >=25% fewer full bytes than independent adapter bank, and strict quality/byte gain over native rank-2 coefficient-table control.
failure_gate: FAIL on byte miss, heldout sequence quality miss, or exact native coefficient factorization alias.

compute.mac_proxy: 64 per shared core application plus 128 per two rank-1 atom coefficients; count each option application in a sequence

boundaries: Synthetic linear option maps only; no trained recurrent motor controller, robot, simulator, or safety claim.
Option sequence IDs are known and charged.
Off-span option is included to measure need for private capacity; no audit seeds are opened after frozen gate failure.
